questions.q: What is the cell theory, and how do prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells differ?

answer.text: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life. The cell theory, put forward by Schleiden and Schwann and completed by Virchow, states that all living things are made of cells, that the cell is the basic unit of life, and that all new cells arise from pre-existing cells. Robert Hooke first observed cells in cork in 1665.
These, as in bacteria, are simple cells that lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; their genetic material lies free in the cytoplasm.
These, found in plants, animals and fungi, have a true nucleus enclosing the genetic material and many membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria.

questions.q: Describe the main organelles of a cell and their functions.
answer: A cell contains several organelles, each with a special function.

answer.text: The plasma membrane is selectively permeable and controls what enters and leaves the cell, while plant cells also have a rigid cell wall of cellulose.
The nucleus controls all the cell's activities and contains the chromosomes, which carry the genes.
Mitochondria are the powerhouse, releasing energy through respiration, and chloroplasts in plant cells carry out photosynthesis.
Ribosomes make proteins, the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus transport and package materials, lysosomes digest waste, and vacuoles, large in plant cells, store substances.
